answer: Each agent receives a limited, nontransferable admission credential after a person completes a costly uniqueness check, such as an in-person liveness session; the credential signs the agent’s actions but cannot be copied to another account. A bridge contract rejects trades without a valid signature and prevents one credential from claiming multiple identities. An attacker can still recruit real people, but must pay for each check and credential, so mass fake identities become expensive. A lotus or quill name alone grants no admission.
